verdicts.note: No abstract; pregnancy among runaway and homeless young women.
Sociocultural fertility determinants among the Soninke in the Gambia.
Household characteristics including LIVING ARRANGEMENTS against child nutritional status across countries. Arrangement as exposure, child health as outcome.

SIBLING differences in marriage timing in the rural Netherlands 1860-1940, using within-family resource allocation. Pre-modern, and the within-family design is a template for holding parental resources fixed.
Oslo youth's future orientations and individualisation.
Editorial on family processes in paediatric psychology.
How far parental social background shapes DEMOGRAPHIC behaviour -- leaving home among the outcomes -- as distinct from socioeconomic outcomes. Link 1's stratification question.
Resilience among destitute Indian adolescents.
Law review on minor parents' parental rights.

NOTABLE FOR ITS DESIGN. Uses grandparents' LIVING STATUS rather than their care provision precisely because grandparental care may be ENDOGENOUS -- care responds to the fertility it is supposed to cause. That is §3's anticipation problem recognised inside the C.2.a literature, and the fix is the shape this chapter needs. Exposure is still kin availability, so C.2.a's, but read it for the strategy.
Falling fertility driving household size and income distribution in Uruguay.

South Korean intergenerational co-residence, arguing it is structured by DEMOGRAPHIC change as well as norms -- mortality decline raises exposure to the 'risk' of co-residence. The availability constraint again, now for a contemporary Asian setting.
Narrative account of women's autonomy in Indian joint families, with parents-in-law driving sex-selective decisions. D.2.c's; ethnographic.
Italian Cassazione ruling on surrogacy.
No abstract; PATRILOCAL marriage and domestic violence in Tajikistan. Arrangement as exposure, violence as outcome.
Young adults recalling living with grandparents in childhood; development outcome.
Family composition and healthcare utilisation among elderly Nigerians.
Encyclopedia entry on families in Canada.
Encyclopedia entry on the EMPTY NEST and the supposed syndrome. The parents'-side construct named and historicised; useful for the §6 vocabulary section.
Vehicle ownership near suburban metro stations.
HOUSING multigenerational households in Sydney and Brisbane. The dwelling stock as the constraint on the arrangement -- Wall 1 from the built-environment side.
Essay on population and environment.

Taipei household transitions in the PSFD panel, with one of the modelled groups being households MOVING FROM LIVING WITH PARENTS TO RENTING. Prices, commuting cost and the arrangement in one multinomial logit -- the same Taiwanese panel as the housing-options record in batch 17.
No abstract; long-term care needs among older persons in Myanmar.

Extension of early adulthood in IRELAND and the 'unbundling' of the transition to independent household formation from tightly ordered mid-century sequencing. States the de-sequencing that §3 has to model.
Lay accounts of modern versus traditional family in Cairo. D.1.b's developmental idealism.

Links the TIMING OF MARRIAGE to CORESIDENCE and CHILDBEARING across European countries and the US, extending Holland's marriage typology. All three events in one framework, cross-nationally -- descriptive, but it is the map of the sequence the chapter has to explain.
Maine law on de facto parenthood.

RETURNING to the parental home in FRANCE at different life stages, including returns after 30, and what motivates leaving versus returning. The boomerang half of link 1, with an older population than the British studies.
Child malnutrition in Angola.
Resilience and school behaviour in Ecuadorian primary pupils.
No abstract; household life cycle and slums in Bangalore.

No abstract; impact of SOCIAL PENSIONS on intergenerational relationships in China, comparative. Companion to the pension RD in batch 16 -- the same policy variation, and together they are the best-identified driver-to-arrangement evidence in the frame.
Theory of planned behaviour and adolescent drug use in Iran.
Grandparents' childcare determining mothers' labour force participation in China. C.2.a's exposure, labour-supply outcome -- the two route-outs at once.

Evolution of the ORDER of four family life events -- LEAVING THE PARENTAL HOME, first cohabitation, first marriage, FIRST PARENTHOOD -- across twentieth-century Europe, using ESS and GGP microdata. The sequencing question at its most direct; §3's problem measured as a changing order rather than assumed.
No abstract; division of domestic labour and lowest-low fertility in South Korea. D.2.a's.
Editorial on ageing and cardiovascular disease.
Church affiliation and life-course transitions across 30,000 reconstructed Dutch life courses 1850-1970. Denomination as a pre-determined driver of the transition sequence; D.1.a seam, historical.
Burnout among paediatric residents.
Icelandic review of parents' needs caring for technology-dependent children at home.
Early life-course events and volunteering in late life.
Intergenerational solidarity between older parents and adult children in China.

CHILDCARE ARRANGEMENTS and the risk of SECOND BIRTH in the UK, including a preference for grandparental care. Exposure is the care arrangement rather than co-residence; C.2.a's, and a parity-specific fertility outcome makes it a close boundary case.
No abstract; the 'kinship penalty', parenthood and in-law conflict in Finland.
Childhood maltreatment and the transition into motherhood.
Essay on Malthus. C.4.a's.
Characteristics of divorced individuals in Turkey.
Tubal ligation at caesarean section.
No abstract; benefit systems and marriage dissolution.

'Produzeni zivot mladih s roditeljima' -- the EXTENDED LIVING OF YOUNG PEOPLE WITH PARENTS, its drivers and its consequences, in a Balkan setting. The pre-launch construct as the whole subject; consequences named but not obviously including births.
Health literacy in orthopaedic patients.
Family instability and child wellbeing in Fragile Families.
Son preference and fertility choices in Cooch Behar; patrilocality as a premise. D.2.c's.

Orphanhood status, LIVING ARRANGEMENTS and SEXUAL DEBUT among southern African adolescent girls. The arrangement is the exposure and the outcome is first sex -- an A.14 outcome, one step short of a birth, in a population where children commonly live apart from parents.
